text:
sam: quick question — when we talk about consolidating the adapter surface for hosted/dedicated/private, are we comfortable introducing a small explicit 'handshake' token to avoid credential leakage across fallbacks?

ana: +1 to narrowing the surface. can you sketch the threat you're worried about?

sam: threat: when runtime falls back from hosted->dedicated, we currently proxy credentials in full. that means dedicated infra momentarily has access to longer-lived KMS blobs. wanted to see if we prefer: 1) short-lived session tokens with limited scope, or 2) masking and re-requesting secrets from control plane on each handoff.

kumar: option (1) seems simpler operationally. we can mint an adapter-scoped session TTL=15s token that allows only model-serving ops. no KMS unwrap.

liz: curious about failure scenarios: if the session token can't be minted (control plane unreachable), do we fail closed or allow a degraded fallback using cached creds?

sam: good point. my thought: fail closed for sensitive ops (eviction, secret rebind) and allow read-only inference with cached, audited keys for a short window. need clear telemetry so we can detect cached-key usage.

ana: propose a tiny capability manifest passed at handshake time. example: 
```
capability_manifest:
  scope: serve-only
  allow_evict: false
  allowed_models: [redwood-v1, llama-2-q]
  token_ttl: 15s
```
this avoids giving broader privileges to the target runtime.

kumar: +1. also add `audited:true` flag and require runtime to emit `orig_handshake_id` in traces so we can trace which control-plane request originated the session.

liz: operationally we need fallback rules: if handshake fails, route to secondary hosted region OR return 503 depending on customer tier. we mustn't silently downgrade to cached creds without alerting.

sam: agree — SLA tier drives fallback: free-tier -> 503 with clear error; paid/enterprise -> try secondary region, then can allow cached read-only with audit.

deploy-bot: deploy check: handshake-token-mint-service tests failing in staging (403 on ephemeral creds) — @kumar can you take a look? :gear:

kumar: on it. I think the 403 is from the token policy change we pushed yesterday. will revert policy for staging and add a stricter integration test.

ana: next steps: 
- @kumar: prototype session token mint + audited trace ID (ETA EOD Wed)
- @sam: draft a short RFC describing manifest fields and fallback policy (ETA Fri)
- @liz: define telemetry/alerting rules for cached-creds fallback (ETA Thu)

sam: one more note — keep the surface minimal: the runtime should only accept `session_token` and `capability_manifest` fields. avoid adding raw secret blobs to the handshake.

liz: ack. thanks all. this should remove a lot of accidental privilege expansion during mode handoffs. :+1:

kumar: quick config snippet I'll prototype: 
```yaml
handshake_request:
  session_token: <jwt>
  manifest: <signed-manifest>
  orig_handshake_id: "${uuid()}"
```

sam: perfect. file RFC and cc security.

liz: ping when tests are green.
